title_vi: Frankenstein, hay Prometheus thời hiện đại
translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: The 1818 first-edition text is translated, not the revised 1831 text; the unsigned Preface, the Milton epigraph and the dedication are included.
decisions.rationale: The first edition is the selected witness.

decisions.decision: The Milton epigraph and the Coleridge, Percy Shelley and Wordsworth quotations are rendered as Vietnamese verse with the same number of lines.
decisions.rationale: The quotations are part of the novel’s texture.

decisions.decision: Walton’s frame letters keep their date lines, salutations and signatures as separate units; Walton writes to his elder sister as em/chị.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: nó used for William, Ernest and Elizabeth in Alphonse’s letter and Clerval’s speech; now reserved for the creature, and the miniature disambiguated.
“my creator” no longer contemptuous (kẻ) in the creature’s pleas; kẻ kept only for curses.
The wedding-night threat made verbatim with the source’s punctuation at every recurrence.
Felix as chàng throughout; ‘cousin’ restored in Elizabeth’s address; chái kept only for the hovel; ‘Great God!’ as Lạy Chúa!; Victor’s father ông in narration.
‘large assemblages of men’, ‘does not grudge’, ‘fatal’ and ‘my friend’ corrected; calques in 145, 181, 322, 338, 501, 538, 588 recast; last sentence strengthened.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: fiend / dæmon / wretch / monster / creature / being
glossary.draft_rendering: con quỷ / ác quỷ / kẻ khốn khổ / quái vật / sinh vật (tạo vật in relation to its creator)
glossary.rationale: Shelley’s shifting names for the creature are kept distinct; sinh linh is reserved for human beings.

glossary.draft_rendering: ta / ngươi in face-to-face confrontations; tôi / ông in the creature’s narrated tale
glossary.rationale: Mirrors the source’s own shift between thou and you.

glossary.source_term: “I will be with you on your wedding-night”
glossary.draft_rendering: Ta sẽ ở bên ngươi trong đêm tân hôn của ngươi
glossary.rationale: The threat recurs verbatim, with the source’s punctuation, every time it is quoted.
Victor’s brothers and Elizabeth are never nó, so the pronoun keeps its weight.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #41445, transcribed from a photo-reprint of the first edition (London: Lackington, Hughes, Harding, Mavor & Jones, 1818), in three volumes. The more widely used Gutenberg #84 reproduces the revised 1831 text and was not used. Not collated with a print facsimile.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The unfinished female creature is called ả in Victor’s reasoning, sharper than the source’s neutral she.

title_review.target_title: Frankenstein, hay Prometheus thời hiện đại
title_review.rationale: Frankenstein, hay Prometheus thời hiện đại keeps Shelley’s double title; hay reproduces the source’s ‘; or,’.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Milton epigraph and dedication from the title pages.
Coleridge, Mutability and Wordsworth stanzas kept as verse.
